payload.analysis: Barium swallow demonstrates cricopharyngeal hypertrophy with thumbprint sign and bar, and postoperative imaging shows bar resolution without leak. Biopsy confirms myopathic changes including endomysial fibrosis, adipose deposition, fiber size variation, internal nuclei, and rare necrotic fibers with negative stains. Distal dilations gave only partial relief, and absence of odynophagia, hematemesis, or active mucosal inflammation argues against GERD and structural esophageal disease. These findings establish cricopharyngeal dysfunction and myopathy as the primary cause. Manometry, VFSS, and endoscopy reports remain unavailable, but current evidence sufficiently supports the diagnosis; all retrievable key imaging information has been integrated.

payload.report: The patient has >10-year dysphagia. Barium swallow showed cricopharyngeal hypertrophy/bar; intraoperatively the cricopharyngeus was thick; biopsy showed myopathic changes with nonnecrotizing granulomas; postoperative barium showed bar resolution. These strongly support cricopharyngeal myopathy/hypertrophy as the mechanism of cricopharyngeal dysfunction. Structural esophageal disease and active GERD inflammation were excluded by imaging/pathology and clinical findings. Nonnecrotizing granulomas raise sarcoidosis-associated myopathy, but serum ACE/calcium/chest CT are pending, so it remains unconfirmed. Missing manometry/VFSS limit full exclusion of other UES-opening causes, but current evidence makes cricopharyngeal myopathy/hypertrophy the best explanation.
